**Project Milestone 1: Develop the First Draft of the Project Proposal**

## **1\. Project Title**

**Project Name:**  
*(Provide a concise and descriptive title for your proposed application/project.)*

**School-Based Lost and Found Tracking System**

---

## **2\. Brief Description**

*(Provide a short overview of the project. Describe what the application is, its purpose, and what users can do with it.)*

**Description:**

Our project focuses on making an organized, school-wide Lost and Found Tracking System for the PSHS-SRC campus. Its purpose is to help students, teachers, and school personnel locate misplaced belongings without having to physically visit different lost and found areas across the campus. Users can report lost or found items by providing relevant information, such as the item’s description, location, and date. The system will also allow users to search for reported belongings and submit ownership claims. For items, claimants must provide accurate descriptions of their belongings’ physical characteristics for verification by authorized personnel before the items can be released.

**3\. Problem Statement**

*(Describe the problem, need, or situation that your project aims to address. Explain why the application is needed.)*

**Problem Identified:** 

Students sometimes misplace their personal belongings within the school campus, such as water bottles, bags, notebooks, gadgets, and other school supplies. Finding these belongings can be difficult because lost and found items are kept in different locations around the campus, such as Academic Building 2, the Guard House, the Library, and other areas. Students may need to travel across the school grounds and check each location individually to find their missing belongings, which can be time-consuming and inconvenient.

Furthermore, the lack of a centralized system makes it difficult for students to check if their missing belongings have been found. Valuable items, including normal items, also require ownership verification to prevent unauthorized claims. Thus, a digital tracking system is needed to make reporting, searching, and claiming items easier and more secure.

**Target Users / Beneficiaries:**

## The target users or beneficiaries are the people present in PSHS-SRC in KC, particularly students, teachers, and school personnel. 

## **4A. Outline of Features**

*(List and describe the main features of your application. Ensure that the proposed features make meaningful use of persistent data—data that is stored and can be accessed again even after closing the application.)*

| Feature | Description | Persistent Data Used |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Logging of Lost and Found Items | Allows users to register a lost or found item with an item name, description, when and where it was found. | Saves each new item's details into an items list/array so the data stays saved even after the program closes.  |
| Search index / Item library | Allows users of this program to search for any logged / registered items. | Loads and reads all saved items from items list/array so users can view or search past entries.  |
| Item Selection and Claiming  | Allows users to select an item by its index number from the list to view full details and mark it as **"**Claimed**"**. | Updates the item's status to "Claimed" directly inside the items array so the change is saved permanently.  |
|  Returned Items Log  | Maintains a permanent audit trail of all items that have been successfully returned to their owners.   | Copies/saves claimed items into a separate history array for long-term record keeping.   |
| Claim Verification | Before claiming the item this will ask the user for details that their item may/may not have so that it can prevent others from stealing an item they didn’t actually own. | Stores verification questions, distinct item marks, or security pins directly inside a parallel verification array (or as extra elements within the items array) when the item is first logged, allowing the system to cross-check user inputs before changing the status to "Claimed".  |

## **4B. Data Design**

**Item List/Arrays**

* **item\_names:** Stores the name or title of the lost or found item (e.g., "Black Hydro Flask", "Leather Wallet").  
* **item\_descriptions:** Stores general, publicly visible details such as color, brand, and size shown in the search index.  
* **item\_dates:** Stores the date and time when the item was found or reported lost.  
* **item\_locations:** Stores the specific place or room where the item was found or last seen.  
* **item\_statuses:** Stores the current state of the item, set to "Unclaimed" when first logged and updated to "Claimed" once returned.  
* **verification\_details:** Stores hidden security info such as distinct item marks, secret contents inside the item, verification questions, or a security PIN which is used to verify ownership before claiming.

   **Returned Items History Arrays**

* **history\_item\_names:** Stores the name of each item that passed verification and was successfully claimed.  
* **history\_claimants:** Stores the name or ID of the person who verified ownership and claimed the item.  
* **history\_dates\_claimed:** Stores the date when the item was officially claimed and returned.  
* **history\_locations:** Stores the original location where the claimed item was found for reference and tracking.

## **5\. Sample Wireframe of the Application**

**Wireframe / Flowchart Area:![][image1]**

VIEW LIBRARY SECTION : Pressing claim in the view library section redirects the user to the claiming panel.

**![][image2]**

Pressing the “Log in” button in the interface screen redirects the user to this panel.

**![][image3]**

**Screen Description:**

* Screen 1: This screen serves as the main interface of the Lost and Found application. It displays the application title and provides three main navigation buttons: History, Log In, and View Library. These buttons allow users to access previously recorded activities, register found items, and browse the list of reported belongings. On the top right corner, the program’s location is set to default / where the program was installed.

* Screen 2: This screen displays the view Library interface, which contains a scrollable list of registered lost and found items. Each entry includes an item’s picture (if provided, if there are no provided pictures upon registration of the item – the system assigns a preview set by a monitor/staff of the program), name, assigned code, and the name of the person who registered it. Users can use the search bar to find specific items and select the Claim button to begin the claiming process. Selecting an item’s additional information also allows users to view more details about it.

* Screen 3:  This screen displays the Log In interface, where users enter their name (full name registration is required) , provide the item’s name and picture(optional), and fill in additional details about the found item. It also displays an automatically assigned item code and registration date. Once all necessary information is provided, users can press the Register button to submit the item’s record to the system.
